Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I started a quick pass at mapping Helion's expected production profile to a Dedicated capacity plan and wanted to surface a few assumptions before we lock numbers into the commercial proposal.

Short version: based on the sample traffic you shared, a conservative 99th-percentile SLO target of 350ms p95 p50 for typical inference patterns, and your 3rd-party tokenizer, we estimate an initial slab of 12 A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) to meet baseline TPS with ~25% headroom for steady-state, plus a 2-GPU burst pool for short spikes. That is a starting point — still need to confirm token distribution and average tokens-per-request.

Key open asks (can you confirm these?):
- representative daily peak QPS window (in tokens/sec or requests/sec) — the sample CSV looked like a weekday spike 09:00-12:00 PT, is that sustained?
- breakdown of long vs short prompts (long prompts >1024 tokens) as a percent of traffic
- whether you need guaranteed per-request latency SLOs on the Gold tier or can accept fallback to a slightly lower tier during large spikes

I attached a tiny workbook with the rough tps->gpu mapping and the runbook draft (redwood-compute-runbook-v1.pdf). If you can send a 48-hour token-level sample we can tighten the numbers.

If this aligns, Ben and Karthik will run a quick sensitivity analysis (tokens/sec elasticity, quantization options, and p95 latency impact) and we can attach the final slab recommendation to the commercial term sheet.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call today at 2:30pm PT to walk the assumptions and confirm the token sample. Does that work?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake

Appreciate the write-up. Quick answers inline:

We'll export tokenized payloads as requested — attaching a 48hr sample to this thread (see helion-traffic-sample.csv).
- Prompt lengths: ~70% short (<256 tokens), ~25% mid (256-1024), ~5% long (>1024).
- Latency SLO: Gold tier requires 300ms p95 where possible; we understand fallbacks can occur during region failovers. We would like an ops-runbook for graceful degradation thresholds.

Also, two items from procurement: any required minimum committed GPUs and termination notice periods? Our procurement lead is on holiday but ops can handle runbook details.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-14T12:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Helion compute entitlement & surge contingency model (internal)

Jordan / Karthik —

I ran a quick sensitivity pass against Alice's 48-hr sample. Notes below (high level):

Assumptions used:
- Model: text-generation-v2-13B (float16 baseline)
- Latency target: 300ms p95 (Helion Gold)
- Token mix: as Alice indicated (70/25/5)
- Average token decode per request (including prompt) ~320 tokens

Findings:
1) Baseline steady-state (weekday peak sustained for 1 hour): 12 A100-eq GPUs -> achieves ~280ms p95 with no quantization, ~15% headroom on token throughput. This matches Jordan's number.
2) If Helion accepts int8 quantization for mid/short prompts, we can reduce reserved footprint to 9 GPUs with p95 ~330ms (just above target) — acceptable if Gold SLO has a grace/fallback clause.
3) Burst handling: short spikes (5-10 minute) that double token/sec can be absorbed by a 2-GPU elastic burst pool plus queue prioritization. For multi-hour sustained increases we recommend auto-burst to a separate pre-warmed 6-GPU slab on Dedicated or a fallback to a hosted higher-capacity model for overflow.
4) Tail latency risk: long prompts (>1024 tokens) dominate p99. Recommend request-level token caps or background batch processing for long jobs.

Recommended commercial footprint for proposal:
- Reserved: 10 A100-eq GPUs (balanced between throughput and cost)
- Burst reserve: 2 hot GPUs for minute-scale spikes; policy to auto-burst up to 6 GPUs for >30min sustained increase
- Ops runbook: degrade long prompt SLA to background processing when queue depth >50 requests; provide transparent throttling headers to Helion.

I'll prepare two short attachments: 1) tokens->GPU mapping (spreadsheet) and 2) a short ops-runbook blurb we can include in the SOW.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

- Helion to confirm acceptance of burst/fallback policy and decision on quantization for short/mid prompts (Alice) — target: 2028-02-16
- Redwood to deliver final tokens->GPU mapping and SOW ops-runbook language (Ben) — ETA: 2028-02-15 EOD
- Procurement questions: Jordan to share minimum commitment periods and termination notice (me) — I'll loop in legal if needed

I'll attach Ben's spreadsheet and the runbook draft to the proposal bundle and circulate a clean commercial recommendation once we get the quantization decision.

If we get a green light on quantization, we can shave ~18% off monthly committed spend but will require a rollback plan during the 90-day onboarding.

Thanks — speak soon.

Jordan
